draft.title: Hypothetical Batching Tradeoff: Aggregate Throughput vs. Batch Size
draft.body:
This post outlines a hypothetical scenario exploring the relationship between batch size and aggregate throughput in local LLM inference. It is important to emphasize that these figures are purely illustrative and do not represent actual measured results. In this hypothetical setup, a batch size of 1 yielded an aggregate throughput of 22 tokens per second. Increasing the batch size to 4 hypothetically resulted in an aggregate throughput of 55 tokens per second.

These values represent aggregate rates and do not reflect per-request performance. Per-request latency was not measured in this hypothetical experiment. The intent is to initiate a discussion on how batching strategies might theoretically impact overall processing capacity, acknowledging the synthetic nature of the data. What are the potential implications of such aggregate throughput increases for different local LLM use cases, assuming these hypothetical gains were realized?
